kept.reason: No assertion maps: this test checks which of several session files in a worktree speaks (start order, end order, both read orders), probed once at 60 min; admission::silence_counts_from_the_end_of_the_last_turn checks the silent bound's timing (30 min working, 31 min silent with its why) on one session. The shared lines are World::working and the session write; folding the 30/31 timeline into silent_with's single 60-min probe changes what each case checks.

Setups conflict: all three of its cases start from a merge red (red_on_moved_proving) and check the moved-proving rule (same tip; proving moved but red tip not merged; red tip merged then gate red). The other test starts from a gate red and checks first-red handling (worker told, proving unchanged, issue ready) and then a gate-red second. No assertion maps, and each case needs its own World, so folding saves no setup and would change which first red each case checks.
Checks the restart, the proof on a copy of the db and another formula's cut leaving the daemon; the stale-link test sets brew.stale_link, a different install path, and asserts none of these.

Asserts the reused promotion clone's origin/HEAD and pruned branches; promote_and_cut_by_hand checks commit identity and hand runs on another flow; no assertion maps, and folding refs edits into it would change its landings.
Asserts hand promote/cut answers, commit authors from host gitconfig and the tag on the step's commit; the busy cut test asserts only the cut bound edge.
Red slow gate: base held, finding, no re-gate on the same tip, by-hand regate, then a fixed tip promoted; the path scenario runs a green slow gate and asserts none of this.
Asserts a reused promotion clone fetches origin's new tags (gates run git describe); the promotion test asserts nothing about tags or clones.

Asserts the lock holder is named from ps and others are not, and 7 upgrades; the upgrade-failure test sets brew.refuses, a conflicting brew state.

Asserts a base pushed by hand turns promotion red and is not moved over; the red-output test asserts gate output files and retention; nothing maps.

stale_link: one link --overwrite and PATH resolves to the new keg; the lock-holder test asserts lock handling; conflicting brew states.

kept_files.reason: deepened by factorium#93 (docs/adr/0003): one pass for the tick, two moves for the owner, the cut in line/cut.rs; no commit has touched it since, its churn predates that change

deepened by factorium#91 (docs/adr/0001): model() lives here beside App::open on purpose, so each new domain command adds one line here; churn since (#113, #119, #128) is those lines plus #119's HostClock adapter beside Engine::new, no new concept

The tick is the composition root: pass() orders every step that moves without a command (idle, lines, bumps, worker health, one admitted start, resume, watch look, swap), and each step's rules already live behind deeper modules (line.rs via lines(), load.rs, swap.rs, issues.rs blockers, domain admission/bump/worker). Its interface is small: tick/run/stop/daemon_start, and scenarios test through tick() only. Churn is features adding one step each, which belong in the pass's order here; daemon.rs was already deepened by factorium#93 (lines) and #134 (swap). Moving bumps/next_issue/resume_parked out would only relocate one-call private helpers, not add depth.

Deep already: callers (gate.rs, line/cut.rs, idle.rs, daemon.rs) use one entry, heavy(Job, Turn), plus Job's per-kind constructors and the tick hooks asking_once/beside/adopt_queued/note_rules; behind it sit queueing, place-keeping, stale-rules exec, dead-pid cleanup, session noting, hold-bound and give-way ending. Deletion test: removing it would spread that protocol over its four callers. Rules already live in factorium_domain::heavy; no unit tests reach past the interface (covered by queue/admission scenarios). Churn is feature work on the queue (factorium#193/#194), not interface friction. factorium#206
